quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and then proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol harm your reflexes and judgment the same way. The only thing that matters is how much alcohol you have consumed.

questions.question: What does a sign with a red circle and a slash through it mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
You must yield to other drivers.
You must drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means something is not allowed. These signs are rectangular, white, and have red and black markings. A red circle and slash on a black symbol means that action is forbidden.

questions.question: When driving on the frontage road of a controlled-access highway, when must you yield the right-of-way?

options.text: To a vehicle entering or about to enter the frontage road from the highway.
To a vehicle leaving or about to leave the frontage road to enter the highway.
Both of the above.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to vehicles entering the frontage road from the highway. You must also yield to vehicles leaving the frontage road to enter the highway.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to park your vehicle?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn drivers about railroad crossings. This sign tells you to watch for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It causes hearing loss.
It causes pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It causes poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic fumes from your vehicle. A leak allows carbon monoxide gas to enter the passenger area. Fix leaks right away to stay safe.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger directs you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when told to by a flagger, stop sign, or warning lights and gates. Some crossings do not have these devices. Never drive around lowered crossing gates—it is illegal.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to pedestrians still in the intersection.
Accelerate as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians still in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let any pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start from the left lane when turning left on a multilane street or highway.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than the traffic around them. Drive at the same speed as other vehicles, but always stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go through.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only turn in the direction of the arrow. Only proceed if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Mirrors alone cannot see your blind spots.

questions.question: What should you do if your car breaks down on a highway?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down on a highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Move as far off the road as possible and lift your hood so other drivers know your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a hospital emergency room is located to the right.

questions.question: What must you do when a bus signals to return to the road after stopping?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield to the bus.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the bus.
questions.explanation: When a bus signals to return to the road after picking up passengers, you must yield. Slow down, move to another lane, or stop to let the bus safely enter the traffic.

questions.question: How are bicycles treated on the road?

options.text: They must always give way to cars.
They do not have to follow traffic rules.
They have the same rights and responsibilities as cars.
They are not a safety concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have the same rights and responsibilities as cars.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as cars. Drivers must respect the rights of people riding bicycles.

questions.question: What should you do if your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking hard and carefully steer back onto the road. Watch for other traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a suggested driving speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit. In bad weather or poor conditions, always slow down.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many accidents happen because drivers do not see motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians. These are smaller and harder to spot than cars because of their size and lighting.

questions.question: What traffic light comes after a steady yellow light?

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Cross carefully only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only continue if a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Follow all instructions from a flagger if one is present.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other cars.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other objects on the road.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It increases.
It decreases.
It stays the same.
It improves.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your field of vision gets smaller. Try to see as much as possible around you when driving.

questions.question: On a two-lane road with no bike lane, how do you safely pass a bicyclist?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bike.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bike.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would pass any other vehicle, but leave at least 3 feet of space (or 5 feet on faster roads). Do not honk unexpectedly as it may startle the rider.

questions.question: When driving in rain, what lights must you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: When can you carefully drive through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through carefully.
